subject: Question about modeling categorical variables in INLA

messages.author: 6b8a5a035983f03e
messages.subject: Question about modeling categorical variables in INLA
parts:
Hi,

I have begun working with a new dataset in R-INLA and have two covariates in my model that are categorical variables, including age (adult and yearling) and sex (male and female). 

I am using inla.stack and the inla formula as follows:

StackEst <- inla.stack(data = list(y=data$Result),

A = list(A_point, 1),

effects = list(c(s.index, list(Intercept = 1)),
list(Sex = data$sex,
       Age = data$age)),
tag = "Est")

formula < y ~ -1 +  Sex + Age + f(spatial.field2, model = spde1)

When I run the above formula and view the summary of results, inla removes one level for sex, but retains both for age.

I have tried using the expand.factor.strategy = "inla" and assigning one of the levels of the variables to NA, but then I received an error in contrasts message saying that contrasts can only be applied to factors with 2 or more levels.

I have tried the following formula to account for the categorical variables and it runs no problem.  

formula < y ~ -1 + f(Sex, model = "iid",  constr = T) + f(Age, model = "iid",  constr = T)  + f(spatial.field2, model = spde1)

Question:
Is accounting for the categorical variables by using (model="iid", constr = T), the best option in this situation, or is there a way to run the model by having one of the levels of each of the categorical variables removed?

Thanks,

Kristin

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Question about modeling categorical variables in INLA
parts:
I would suggest turning your binary factors into binary 0/1 indicator variables instead, since you say you only want to keep one of the two levels from each.
Making explicit 0/1 is the simplest way to control that.

You also need to add + Intercept to your formula if you want to include it in the model (you have it in the stack).

Finn
